rationale: The governing SPEC lives in the private ../project-specs tree, absent from this submodule checkout and from CI. The committed requirements.tsv / standards.tsv are frozen and independently consistency-checked by check_catalogs; the drift check is a generator sanity check, not a requirement verification.
Captures the host locale list for the availability probe; the trailing || true only avoids a nonzero exit when the list is empty. Not a gate step and not a normative leg.

C and POSIX (the two mandatory profiles) are always present and always run. The UTF-8 locales are best-effort on dev hosts; CI sets SV0_STRINGS_REQUIRE_LOCALES so a missing en_US.UTF-8 / tr_TR.UTF-8 is a hard failure there, never a skipped normative leg.

Emitted only when a test/expectations.tsv row's c_exit is the literal SKIP; there are zero such rows today. Reserved for a legitimately VM-only fixture, which would carry its own rationale in that row's note column.

VM project mode has no contract-mode selector (SPEC OQ-012 / UP-028); a non-runtime request is reported unsupported rather than faked. The default gate runs contract-mode=runtime so this never triggers; SS-185's verified/disabled matrix records unsupported distinctly and never counts it as a pass.

Local-dev convenience when the cc lacks -fsanitize=address,undefined. CI sets SV0_STRINGS_REQUIRE_SANITIZERS=1, which turns this into a hard failure, so release evidence always contains the sanitizer run.

Apple's ASan has no LeakSanitizer and aborts if detect_leaks is forced on. Linux CI runs with leak detection enabled, so the leak evidence is produced there; macOS is a dev host, not a release-evidence host.
